title: Find Valid Emails
statement:
Each user has one email address on file:

- `Users(user_id, email)`: one row per user; `user_id` is unique.

An email is **valid** when all of these hold:

- it has exactly one `@`;
- the part before the `@` is non-empty and uses only letters, digits and underscores (`_`);
- the part after the `@` is a non-empty run of letters followed by `.com`, which ends the address (so no digits, dots, hyphens or other characters in the domain name).

Return the `user_id` and `email` of every valid address, ordered by `user_id` ascending.
constraints: Letters are A-Z and a-z; digits are 0-9
reference:
SELECT user_id, email
FROM Users
WHERE email REGEXP '^[A-Za-z0-9_]+@[A-Za-z]+\\.com$'
ORDER BY user_id;
brute:
WITH RECURSIVE pos AS (
  SELECT 1 AS p
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p + 1 FROM pos WHERE p < (SELECT MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(email)) FROM Users)
),
parts AS (
  SELECT user_id, email,
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(email, '@', 1) AS local_part,
    SUBSTRING(email, CHAR_LENGTH(SUBSTRING_INDEX(email, '@', 1)) + 2, CHAR_LENGTH(email) - CHAR_LENGTH(SUBSTRING_INDEX(email, '@', 1)) - 5) AS domain
  FROM Users
  WHERE CHAR_LENGTH(email) - CHAR_LENGTH(REPLACE(email, '@', '')) = 1
    AND RIGHT(email, 4) = '.com'
)
SELECT user_id, email
FROM parts
WHERE CHAR_LENGTH(local_part) > 0
  AND CHAR_LENGTH(domain) > 0
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pos
    WHERE pos.p <= CHAR_LENGTH(local_part)
      AND NOT (SUBSTRING(local_part, pos.p, 1) BETWEEN 'a' AND 'z'
        OR SUBSTRING(local_part, pos.p, 1) BETWEEN 'A' AND 'Z'
        OR SUBSTRING(local_part, pos.p, 1) BETWEEN '0' AND '9'
        OR SUBSTRING(local_part, pos.p, 1) = '_'))
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pos
    WHERE pos.p <= CHAR_LENGTH(domain)
      AND NOT (SUBSTRING(domain, pos.p, 1) BETWEEN 'a' AND 'z'
        OR SUBSTRING(domain, pos.p, 1) BETWEEN 'A' AND 'Z'))
ORDER BY user_id
notes:
## Intuition

Every rule is about the shape of a single string, and together they describe the whole address from its first character to its last: word characters, one `@`, letters, `.com`. A regular expression anchored at both ends states that shape in one condition, and anything that does not fit it exactly (a second `@`, a dot in the user name, a digit in the domain, a different ending) is rejected automatically.

## Approach

1. Read every row of `Users`.
2. Keep the rows whose `email` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+@[A-Za-z]+\\.com$`: `^` and `$` force the pattern to cover the whole address, `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` is the non-empty user name, `@` appears once because neither character class contains it, `[A-Za-z]+` is the letters-only domain name, and `\\.com` is an escaped dot (the doubled backslash in the SQL string reaches the regex as `\.`) followed by `com`.
3. Sort by `user_id`.

## Example 1, step by step

- `alice@example.com`: `alice`, `@`, `example`, `.com`: valid.
- `bob_at_example.com`: there is no `@` at all: invalid.
- `charlie@example.net`: ends in `.net`: invalid.
- `david@domain.com`: valid.
- `eve@invalid`: no `.com` ending: invalid.

The result is users 1 and 4.

## Complexity

- Time: O(N · L) to test N addresses of length up to L, plus sorting the matches.
- Space: O(K) for the K valid rows.

## Pitfalls

- Without `^`, `first.last@example.com` matches on its tail `last@example.com`; without `$`, `a@b.comm` matches.
- In the SQL string the backslash must be doubled (`'\\.com'`) so the regex receives `\.`; an unescaped `.` matches any character, accepting `a@bxcom`.
- `LIKE '%@%.com'` accepts dots, digits and extra `@` signs that the rules forbid.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `^` ... `$` | the pattern must span the whole address |
| `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` | user name: one or more letters, digits or underscores |
| `[A-Za-z]+` | domain name: one or more letters only |
| `\\.com` | a literal dot, then `com` |

narration.1: The output keeps the user id and the address itself.
narration.2: Each user has one address, so every row is checked on its own.
narration.3: The anchored pattern requires word characters, one @, letters only, then .com at the very end.
narration.4: Valid addresses are listed by ascending user_id.
